transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Nice to meet you, Doctor. Well, I came in because... I snapped on a board call recently. It was over a really small question about the facility budget. Just a simple question, but I completely lost my temper. And look, that is just not how I run my company. It's not how I treat people. So, I figured I better come in and see what's going on with me.
Have you noticed other times recently where you've had difficulty controlling your temper or reacting strongly to things, or was this incident on the board call particularly unusual for you?

Honestly, it was pretty unusual. I mean... I can't really think of any other times lately where I've just gone off like that. Sure, running a business gets stressful, but I usually keep a lid on things. That board call... it just came out of nowhere. So, no, I haven't really had trouble controlling my temper besides that one specific time. That's why it bothered me enough to actually come in.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you noticed any changes in your mood overall—like feeling more depressed, more energetic than usual, or more anxious—or has your mood been pretty stable except for that one incident?

Well, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or anxious, really. Just... flat. It's hard to explain. Things that usually settle me down, like working on a chess problem, going over my hiking notes, or even just having a nice dinner with my wife... they just don't do anything for me right now. It's like I know I should be enjoying them, or at least feeling relaxed, but I just can't get there. There's no joy in it lately.
Over the past few weeks, have you experienced any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep than normal, or found yourself taking on a lot of new projects or activities?

No, not at all. I haven't had any bursts of energy or anything like that. I've been sleeping my usual amount, maybe even feeling a little more tired than normal just because of this... flatness I mentioned. And I definitely haven't been taking on any new projects. Honestly, just keeping up with the day-to-day at the company feels like enough right now. So, no, no unusual energy or anything like that.
How long have you been experiencing this flatness and loss of enjoyment in things—is it something that's been going on for a couple of weeks now, or longer?
No, not that long. It's been... about six days. It all started right after the explosion and fire happened during the walkthrough. That's when I first noticed it.
When you say it all started after the explosion and fire during the walkthrough—were you directly involved in that incident, or did you witness it happen?

I was right there. I was doing a routine walkthrough of one of our facilities when a piece of equipment malfunctioned. There was a sudden explosion, and then a fire broke out almost instantly. I was close enough to feel the heat and see the whole thing happen right in front of me.
During that explosion and fire, were you physically injured, or did you feel like your life was in immediate danger?

I wasn't physically injured, thankfully. Just some ringing in my ears for a bit, but no burns or anything. But yes, I absolutely felt like my life was in danger. When that blast went off and the fire shot up... I really thought I might not make it out of there. It happened so fast.
Since the explosion and fire six days ago, have you been having unwanted memories or images of that event popping into your head, or experiencing nightmares about it?

No nightmares, really. But during the day, yes. I'll just be... in the middle of a phone call, or looking at some numbers for work, and the blast and that fire by the loading area just jump back into my head. It's like a bad film I didn't ask to see, just playing right there in my mind.
Have you been trying to avoid things that remind you of the explosion and fire—like avoiding that facility, or avoiding conversations about it, or staying away from anything related to it?

Yeah, I have. I've been keeping away from the new building completely. And it's... well, it's not just the site itself. Even the paperwork is getting to me. The mortgage folder and the safety reports are just sitting on my desk, unopened. The minute I reach for them, my stomach just drops. So I've just been leaving them alone.
Since the explosion six days ago, have you noticed that you're more on edge or jumpy than usual—like startling easily at sudden noises, or feeling like you need to be alert and watching for danger?

Yeah, I've definitely been more jumpy. It's... well, it's just little things that get to me now. If a door shuts hard somewhere in the office, or even if the printer just kicks on suddenly right behind me, I jump like something went off again. My heart starts racing, and it takes me a few minutes just to get my hands steady enough to get back to whatever I was doing. I'm just very on edge.
